scope.focus: voice/wake-word capability temporal lineage and source-level reachability

coverage_credit.reason: Bounded history/code shard; Project-Frankenstein global tree/history denominator is not yet frozen.

lineage.evidence: Initial repository commit explicitly lists voice interaction with wake-word, push-to-talk and local STT.
Commit 5e7f623a removes aicore-voice from frank_watchdog and states wake-word listener disabled; push-to-talk remains functional.
README/HOW_IT_WORKS/persona/self-knowledge changes repeatedly replace wake-word with push-to-talk and remove wake-word references.

Commit 0fd27f adds unified CPU-only FrankVoice with faster-whisper, VAD, TTS and WebSocket voice. The FrankVoice source includes OpenWakeWord detector and an explicit wake_word process mode; WebSocket code handles wake_word action by switching to conversation mode.
Commit 51d6b30d adds faster-whisper and openwakeword to requirements.txt.

At abba90a5 services/frank_voice.py still contains OpenWakeWord ONNX loading, wake_word mode and status; ui/webui/app.py still routes wake_word actions and accepts client-selected voice mode over /ws/voice; requirements.txt still contains openwakeword.

observations.claim: The Feb-19 disable event applies to the legacy aicore-voice watchdog-managed wake daemon, not to a permanent project-wide prohibition on wake-word functionality.
Wake-word functionality was subsequently reintroduced inside the unified FrankVoice architecture rather than by reviving the old aicore-voice daemon.

Frozen-head source evidence establishes a reachable server-side wake_word mode at code level: the WebSocket handler passes mode to FrankVoice, handles wake_word action, and changes to conversation mode after detection.
The detector currently uses OpenWakeWord hey_jarvis_v0.1 as a proxy for 'Hey Frank', threshold 0.5, with fail-closed behavior if model load fails.

Source-level presence and routeability still do not prove that the deployed Frank v0.1 UI selects wake_word mode, that models are installed, or that microphone-to-effect detection works on Andreas' target PC.

synthesis.primary_finding: The apparent wake-word contradiction is a supersession/reintroduction lineage, not simple stale dependency drift: legacy wake daemon disabled -> push-to-talk-only interval -> wake-word reintroduced as an internal FrankVoice mode.
synthesis.frank_v0_1_implication: Self-knowledge should say that current FrankVoice contains optional wake-word support only when runtime/config/effect receipts show it enabled; it must not claim the old aicore-voice daemon is active.

counterhypotheses.claim: openwakeword is merely stale and unused
counterhypotheses.evidence: Frozen-head FrankVoice imports OpenWakeWord lazily, instantiates _WakeWord, exposes wake_word process mode, and WebSocket route handles wake_word action.

counterhypotheses.claim: current end-user UI actually enables wake-word mode
counterhypotheses.next_test: Trace current static frontend controls or run browser/WebSocket interaction; do not infer enabled UI from server capability alone.

counterhypotheses.claim: wake-word works correctly on target hardware
counterhypotheses.next_test: Install/load model and run microphone replay/live detection with positive/negative/near-phrase corpus, latency and false-accept/false-reject measurement.

negative_results: No target-PC runtime effect was executed in this shard.
No claim that wake-word is enabled by default.
No claim that hey_jarvis proxy reliably recognizes 'Hey Frank'.
No exact Level-0 percent or earned-work hours assigned.

tests.name: source-to-runtime reachability
tests.design: Trace frontend mode control -> /ws/voice -> process_chunk(mode='wake_word') -> OpenWakeWord model load -> wake_word event -> conversation transition; record each edge as enabled/reachable/effect-verified.

tests.name: wake phrase calibration
tests.design: Evaluate intended 'Hey Frank', proxy phrase, phonetic near-neighbors, ambient speech and household noise. Measure FAR/FRR, latency and CPU cost; preserve negative results.

tests.name: legacy component falsification
tests.design: Assert aicore-voice daemon remains absent/disabled while FrankVoice wake path can function independently; prevent self-model from conflating the two generations.

tests.name: fail-closed degradation
tests.design: Remove/unavailable OpenWakeWord model/dependency and verify voice PTT/conversation paths continue without false capability reporting or crash.
